title: Prescriptive Learning of Linear Policies with Feasibility Guarantees for Binary Decision-Making
abstract: arXiv:2611.10923v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Binary decision-making under uncertainty arises across a wide range of applications, including energy systems scheduling, transportation, and workforce planning. While machine learning has been increasingly applied to accelerate or replace mixed-integer solvers in such settings, existing approaches rely on predictive learning, training models to reproduce optimal decisions from labeled data, which lacks knowledge of counterfactual outcomes and provides no guarantees that the resulting decisions will be feasible. This limitation is further compounded under distributional shift, where policies trained on historical data may produce systematically infeasible decisions. We propose a prescriptive learning framework for binary decision-making that addresses both limitations. translated_title: 面向二元决策的具有可行性保证的线性策略规范性学习
translated_abstract: 不确定性下的二元决策广泛应用于众多领域，包括能源系统调度、交通运输和人力规划等。尽管机器学习已被越来越多地用于加速或取代此类场景中的混合整数求解器，但现有方法依赖于预测式学习，即训练模型从带标签的数据中复现最优决策，这种方法既缺乏对反事实结果的认知，也无法保证所生成决策的可行性。在分布偏移的情况下，这一局限性会进一步加剧，因为基于历史数据训练的策略可能产生系统性不可行的决策。我们提出了一种面向二元决策的规范性学习框架，以同时解决上述两个局限。该框架不再预测最优标签，而是在所有训练场景上对线性决策策略与可行分配进行联合优化……
tldr: 本文提出一种规范性学习框架，通过在所有训练场景上联合优化线性决策策略与可行分配，为不确定性下的二元决策提供可行性保证，并解决了预测式学习缺乏反事实认知且在分布偏移下易产生不可行决策的问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a prescriptive learning framework that jointly optimizes linear decision policies and feasible assignments across training scenarios, providing feasibility guarantees for binary decision-making under uncertainty while overcoming the counterfactual blindness and distribution-shift infeasibility of predictive learning.
